when: Estimates a composite-based structural model, suited to prediction-oriented research, complex models, and smaller samples.
example: With a small sample and a focus on prediction, PLS-SEM estimates how brand image drives satisfaction and then loyalty, building each idea up from its survey items.
small_sample: PLS-SEM tolerates smaller samples, but the 10-times rule alone is not enough. Justify the size with a power analysis, and report bootstrap confidence intervals for every path.
assumptions: Constructs are modelled as composites of their indicators
Sample size meets the minimum from a power analysis or the inverse square root method, not the 10-times rule alone
Measurement quality is assessed before the structural model: loadings, composite reliability, AVE, and HTMT
Paths are tested with bootstrapped confidence intervals, commonly 5000 resamples
alternative: Covariance-based SEM, for strict theory testing with larger samples
r_code:
# pls_sem_analysis.R
# StatChooser export. Runs with the surveyframe package (Sharafuddin, 2026).
library(surveyframe)

pls_model <- sf_model(
  "pls_1", "Structural model", type = "pls_sem",
  constructs = list(
    sf_construct("IV", "Predictor construct", c("iv_1", "iv_2", "iv_3"),
                 mode = "composite"),
    sf_construct("DV", "Outcome construct", c("dv_1", "dv_2", "dv_3"),
                 mode = "composite")
  ),
  paths   = list(sf_path("IV", "DV")),
  options = list(bootstrap = 5000)
)
syntax <- seminr_syntax(pls_model)
cat(syntax)

# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "pls_sem").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: Predictor construct (IV) ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: Predictor construct (IV)", type = "section_break")
iv_1 <- sf_item("iv_1", "[Predictor item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "iv")
iv_2 <- sf_item("iv_2", "[Predictor item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "iv")
iv_3 <- sf_item("iv_3", "[Predictor item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "iv")
iv <- sf_scale("iv", "Predictor", c("iv_1", "iv_2", "iv_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Section C: Outcome construct (DV) ----
sec_c <- sf_item("sec_c", "Section C: Outcome construct (DV)", type = "section_break")
dv_1 <- sf_item("dv_1", "[Outcome item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "dv")
dv_2 <- sf_item("dv_2", "[Outcome item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "dv")
dv_3 <- sf_item("dv_3", "[Outcome item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "dv")
dv <- sf_scale("dv", "Outcome", c("dv_1", "dv_2", "dv_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Structural model ----
pls_model <- sf_model(
  "model_1", "Structural model", type = "pls_sem",
  constructs = list(
    sf_construct("IV", "Predictor construct", c("iv_1", "iv_2", "iv_3"), mode = "composite"),
    sf_construct("DV", "Outcome construct", c("dv_1", "dv_2", "dv_3"), mode = "composite")
  ),
  paths   = list(sf_path("IV", "DV")),
  options = list(bootstrap = 5000)
)

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, iv_1, iv_2, iv_3, iv, sec_c, dv_1, dv_2, dv_3, dv
  ),
  models        = list(pls_model)
)

# Generate the model syntax:
syntax <- seminr_syntax(pls_model)
cat(syntax)
